direction.comments: The direction on a macroscale is very surreal and absurdist, making the movie feel very Adult Swim-coded; The movie is also pretty political on a grand scale, as it is very much a commentary on capitalism and high fashion; The movie definitely feels like a Boots Riley movie, and it is as if the final 30 minutes of 'Sorry to Bother You' were an entire movie; The direction on a microscale is fine; Storytelling is very absurdist, as the movie really suspends your disbelief and uses wacky ways to move the story forward; The storytelling was a little too weird for my liking; Tension is pretty artificial considering how absurdist the movie is

definitely given the least out of the main three, holds her own and has her moments

cast.comments: The supporting cast fills in these exaggerated, over-the-top characters that paint this surrealist, absurdist world

story.comments: The concept is an absurdist take used to comment on capitalism, kind of throwing shit at the wall to create this abstract painting; The plot structure is pretty linear; Character writing is somewhat present, as you can see the sense of doubt in the protagonist as she juggles her debt; They really do paint very absurdist characters to make this movie feel memorable

screenplay.comments: The dialogue is tonally true to the movie; The humor is very absurdist but does hit a decent amount, despite how out there it is; The symbolism is very evident, as the whole movie is a critique of capitalism and high fashion; The symbolism is a little too forced, as it feels like they are shoving the message down our throats; The foreshadowing is decent

cinematography.comments: Matches the tone with how surreal and absurdist it is, especially with its wide-angle shots

editing.comments: Uses a lot of sharp cuts to make the movie feel very surreal and absurdist

sound.comments: Makes the movie feel very absurdist and surrealist; Visual effects; Pretty bad to decent; I enjoyed the stop motion, but besides that, it just felt very tacky, and the use of blue screen was very obvious; The visual effects really made this world feel very surreal and absurdist

visual_effects.comments: enjoyed the stop motion, but besides that, it just felt very tacky and the use of blue screen was very obvious; the visual effects really made this world feel very surreal and absurdist

production_design.comments: Really helped make this world feel very absurdist and surreal

makeup.comments: Helped show the high fashion and surrealism of the world

costumes.comments: Helped show the high fashion and surrealism of the world

review.climax: The climax was pretty entertaining and brought closure to the message and the character's personal fight
review.tone: The tone is very surreal and absurdist
review.final_notes: Saw the world premiere at SXSW
review.overall: Overall, Boots Riley's sophomore effort takes the ending of 'Sorry to Bother You' and stretches it out for a full movie as he creates this surrealist and absurdist world that feels very Adult Swim-coded in its presentation, but very political in its messaging as the movie critiques capitalism and high fashion
